findings.note: Item 4 answer lists legal roles ("the owner, a trustee, an executor or administrator, or several heirs who agree") and concludes "Living in the house alone does not give you that authority." No cited claim or ledger claim supports a list of who holds authority to sell or the case-specific conclusion (item cites no claim ids; ledger has none on authority). Remove the role list and the 'living in the house' conclusion, or have Research add a supported claim.

Item 3 states "The statute does not mention hoarding" and answers "Possibly" to whether the city or county can act. No ledger claim (clm:1-4) says what the statute omits or that a city or county may enforce it; clm:2-4 speak only of a health officer or fire chief determination. Either add a ledger claim supporting both points (EVIDENCE_REQUEST to R1) or drop the sentence and reframe 'Possibly' to what clm:1-4 support (conditions listed; whether a home meets them is for the local authority).
Item 2 opens "Not always." (flagged). It is an unsupported frequency word that implies cleanout is not required; plainer wording such as 'It depends on...' would remove the implied rule.
